title: Crescent Deck & Leadership Roundup — Winter Threshold
summary: Quarter-end leadership all-hands focused on year-end operational priorities, a brief incident postmortem (M-110), status of the Private beta, hiring posture for Q1, and a roadmap decision for Dedicated SLAs. Clear next steps assigned for incident follow-up, Private beta timelines, and a headcount plan review.

Elena Park: Update public roadmap blurb & community note (2026-12-21)

Private beta readiness checklist review next Tuesday

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58m
Attendees listed in metadata (leadership + open floor)

[00:00] Jasper Nguyen: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for being here. Elena, do you want to kick us off with the Crescent deck highlights?
[00:28] Elena Park: yeah, thanks Jasper, uh quick agenda: incident postmortem, private beta check, dedicated SLA decision and then hiring + org items. We will leave 15 minutes for open q and a, try to keep remarks tight.
[01:05] Rhea Patel: real quick, for folks tuning in late — M-110 was the region routing issue that impacted hosted inference last month, and Samir's team led the recovery. We'll cover root cause and mitigations.
[01:40] Samir Kapur: yep. Short version — it was a cascade where autoscaler heuristic mis-fired during a traffic spike plus a kernel incompat on a subset of GPUs, um the fallback didn't route to the dedicated pool as expected. Not a capacity shortage exactly, more of a routing and retry pathology.
[02:12] Jasper Nguyen: got it. High-level impact and customer outreach — were there any escalations? Marta?
[02:22] Marta Ruiz: we had five enterprise tickets, two with exec POCs, CS and AM engaged, comms were sent within the hour, customers saw degraded latency (~2x) for 37 minutes, and then restored. No data exposure.
[02:44] Ibrahim Khan: rough estimate for Q4 impact — some credits and OD refunds, low double-digit K, will confirm after full RCA.
[03:05] Elena Park: okay thanks. Samir — what's the short term mitigation and long term fix?
[03:15] Samir Kapur: short term: adjust autoscaler thresholds and ensure fallback routing to compatible model variants. Medium: put a canary for the kernel selector change, add circuit breaker on the route. Long term: more aggressive simulation testing for region failovers.
[03:42] Elena Park: action item: Samir to produce after-action doc by Friday, include roll-forward playbook.
[04:01] Samir Kapur: noted.
[04:10] Elena Park: moving on — Private beta. Rhea?
[04:18] Rhea Patel: Private beta is in closed alpha with three customers. Current blockers: finalizing KMS integration for customer-managed keys, VPC peering flaky in one case and the on-prem installer needs a patch for older GLIBC. We shipped a hotfix yesterday for the installer. Beta readiness is looking good but we need sign-off on the KMS plan.
[04:50] Jasper Nguyen: KMS — are we requiring HSM or KMS optional?
[04:56] Rhea Patel: plan is to support cloud KMS (optional) and HSM for enterprises — default will be bring-your-own-KMS via encrypted key wrapping. Need product & security signoff.
[05:14] Marta Ruiz: security already did preliminary review, but we need the compliance scoping doc to go to legal.
[05:22] Elena Park: Rhea to finish the private beta runbook and ship to leadership by Jan 15.
[05:31] Rhea Patel: yep, I'll include SSO/SAML patterns and audit log retention options.
[05:40] Jasper Nguyen: good. Next — Dedicated SLAs. We have three tradeoffs: lower latency vs cost, reserved pool sizes, and regional redundancy. Finance input? Ibrahim?
[05:56] Ibrahim Khan: from a cost POV, reserving 24/7 dedicated pools increases fixed cost considerably. If we offer 99.9% latency SLO vs 99.99% that's ~30% more infra cost. We can tier: bronze/silver/gold.
[06:15] Samir Kapur: tech note — offering 99.99% for small customers is tough; requires cross-region active-active and double the footprint. We should gate gold for enterprise with larger commitments.
[06:32] Jasper Nguyen: sounds like tiered SLA with minimum commit is the play. Elena, product thoughts?
[06:40] Elena Park: agree — we'll draft tiers and standard commitments. Assign pricing to Ibrahim to model.
[06:47] Elena Park: ok quick pulse on hiring: Marta?
[06:51] Marta Ruiz: leadership recommended a temporary hiring posture shift. We're pausing most IC hiring but allowing critical roles (security, infra, key customer success) to continue. Managers to submit exception requests with business case. We'll publish process tomorrow.
[07:10] Jasper Nguyen: we need to be explicit about timelines — how long is this posture?
[07:15] Marta Ruiz: three months review, target reevaluate after Q1 planning.
[07:21] Ibrahim Khan: finance will produce scenarios for headcount at 0%, 5%, and 10% cuts to revenue targets for planning.
[07:30] Elena Park: thanks. Product roadmap: quick hits before year-end and what we defer.
[07:36] Rhea Patel: immediate ship items: private beta hotfixes, model onboarding improvements (faster KV cache warm start) and new quantization path for L4 models. Deferred: full multi-region active-active for Dedicated gold until H1.
[07:56] Jasper Nguyen: sketch the risk — if we defer active-active, enterprise customers may demand on-prem / private options faster. We should emphasize Private product as alternate offering.
[08:10] Rhea Patel: yep, Private will be our lead for regulated customers in short-term.
[08:18] Audience (Speaker 1): any update on the Redwood Optimize tooling?
[08:22] Elena Park: Optimize will go into beta early Q1; it includes autosuggest batching and quantization profiles. Roadmap doc will be posted by Elena post-meeting.
[08:34] Jasper Nguyen: quick financials — Ibrahim?
[08:37] Ibrahim Khan: Q4 bookings trending up 14% YoY but unit economics pressure continues due to GPU pricing. We need to prioritize cost-saving measures: improved batching, caching, and model selection heuristics.
[08:56] Samir Kapur: on the tech side, we have a backlog of kernel optimizations that will improve token throughput by ~10%—we should accelerate that work.
[09:08] Jasper Nguyen: operations & incidents — any notes from on-call?
[09:12] Samir Kapur: yes we've started a weekly inject to test fallback routing. Also adding more observability around kernel selection paths.
[09:23] Elena Park: okay let's open for Q&A, please keep questions concise.

[09:40] Audience: question about support for air-gapped on-prem installs, timeline?
[09:46] Rhea Patel: target for a hardened air-gapped installer is H1; current on-prem will support VPC and limited offline mode but full air-gapped certs and delivery in H1.
[09:58] Audience: will we commit to data residency zones in Europe by next quarter?
[10:04] Ibrahim Khan: we're evaluating Europe region expansion; committed capacity is expensive but doable with enterprise pipeline. We'll publish a roadmap and require customer commitments.
[10:15] Audience: any update on open-source connectors?
[10:19] Elena Park: community PRs have been great, maintainers will be acknowledged in the release notes.
[10:26] Jasper Nguyen: quick aside on culture — Marta, anything to call out?
[10:30] Marta Ruiz: holiday time-off policy reminder, and we will run a mini pulse survey early January to check on manager workload. Also leaders, please nominate folks for the end-of-year recognition.
[10:46] Audience: question re: sales motion—managed vs self-serve, are we shifting?
[10:50] Jasper Nguyen: we remain PLG-first but will couple sales-assisted plays for Dedicated and Private. Self-serve remains primary for hosted API.
[10:59] Rhea Patel: technical note: we need to standardize SDKs and error codes for consistent retries across languages.
[11:10] Samir Kapur: agreed. Tech debt work to standardize client libs is scheduled for Q1.
[11:22] Audience (Speaker 2): are there any upcoming product deprecations?
[11:27] Elena Park: no hard deprecations this cycle. We'll sunset older SDK versions as usual with 60-day notice.
[11:36] Jasper Nguyen: closing items — let's recap next steps. Elena?
[11:40] Elena Park: recap: Samir leads M-110 doc, Rhea finalizes Private beta runbook, Ibrahim shares hiring/budget scenarios, Marta publishes hiring exception process, Elena publishes product blurb, all by dates in the action items.
[11:52] Jasper Nguyen: thanks all. Any last minute?
[11:56] Audience: thumbs up.
[12:00] Jasper Nguyen: okay meeting adjourned. Happy holidays, rest up and we'll reconvene Jan planning.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript with occasional speaker mislabels; some technical terms may be slightly off (e.g., dedcated -> dedicated, SOC two -> SOC 2).
